name: Obed-edom the Gittite
charge: Keeping the ark of God in his house three months, after it had killed Uzzah
summary: Uzzah had just died for touching the ark, and David was afraid to bring it into the city. It went instead into the house of Obed-edom of Gath, and stayed three months. The Lord blessed him and all his household so visibly that David heard of it and came back for the ark with sacrifices and dancing.
offense: After the breach upon Uzzah, David would not bring the ark into the city of David. He carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite, where it remained three months (2 Samuel 6:10-11). The same ark before which judgment had interrupted the procession now stood within a household. The Lord's holiness had not changed; neither had his power to bless. Obed-edom's house received what David had become afraid to bring nearer. Yet the blessing was not a licence to handle the ark however a man pleased. When the journey resumed, the Levites sanctified themselves and carried it upon their shoulders according to the commandment (1 Chronicles 15:12-15). Receiving holy things and observing the order of their service belonged together.
judgment: And the ark of the Lord continued in the house of Obed-edom the Gittite three months: and the Lord blessed Obed-edom, and all his household. It was told king David, saying, The Lord hath blessed the house of Obed-edom, and all that pertaineth unto him, because of the ark of God. The Chronicles count him afterward among the porters and the singers before the ark, with eight sons and sixty-two able men of his house: for God blessed him.
offenseFull: After the breach upon Uzzah, David would not bring the ark into the city of David. He carried it aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite, where it remained three months (2 Samuel 6:10-11). The same ark before which judgment had interrupted the procession now stood within a household. The Lord's holiness had not changed; neither had his power to bless.

Obed-edom's house received what David had become afraid to bring nearer. Yet the blessing was not a licence to handle the ark however a man pleased. When the journey resumed, the Levites sanctified themselves and carried it upon their shoulders according to the commandment (1 Chronicles 15:12-15). Receiving holy things and observing the order of their service belonged together.

entries.commentary: David gathered together thirty thousand chosen men of Israel. Not everyone is a warrior, and not everyone goes to the front lines, but everyone in the body is important in some way; the members that seem more feeble are needful, and on them more honor is bestowed. David and all the people went from Baale of Judah to bring up the ark of God, whose name is called by the name of the Lord of hosts that dwelleth between the cherubims. The ark had been taken from Israel by the Philistines in the days of the judges because of sin, and it had been left in the house of Abinadab. Through the wilderness there had been no house for the Lord, so the ark was moved from place to place. They set the ark upon a new cart, and Uzzah and Ahio, the sons of Abinadab, drove it, with Ahio going before the ark, while David and all the house of Israel played before the Lord on harps, psalteries, timbrels, cornets, and cymbals.

When they came to Nachon's threshingfloor, the oxen shook the cart, and Uzzah put forth his hand and took hold of the ark. The anger of the Lord was kindled, and God smote him for his error, and he died there by the ark. Only chosen men could come near the ark. The Lord had warned Aaron not to come at all times into the holy place before the mercy seat that he die not, and had set many stipulations upon it, even after the two sons of Aaron died for offering strange fire. The Most High is holy and not to be handled carelessly. Grabbing the ark was a natural reaction, but the Most High had already declared it holy and untouchable. Everything in that day had to be done to a T; we owe thanks that there is mercy through Christ, for the Lord was not playing about His commandments. David was displeased that the Lord had made a breach upon Uzzah, and he was afraid of the Lord that day, saying, How shall the ark of the Lord come to me? David had seen the power of the Lord, and his flesh trembled for fear of Him and His judgments. David would not remove the ark to the city of David but carried it aside to the house of Obededom the Gittite, where it remained three months; and the Lord blessed Obededom and all his household because of the ark.

When David heard the Lord had blessed the house of Obededom because of the ark, he went and brought up the ark to the city of David with gladness. When those that bore it had gone six paces, he sacrificed oxen and fatlings. David danced before the Lord with all his might, girded with a linen ephod. He was happy and in the spirit, for the Lord had chosen him to bring the ark back among the people. Israel brought up the ark with shouting and the sound of the trumpet. Michal, Saul's daughter, looked through a window and saw David leaping and dancing before the Lord, and she despised him in her heart. This is a spirit to be careful of: coming out of the spirit on the Lord's day and murmuring against a brother who is rejoicing in the Most High. David set the ark in the tabernacle he had pitched for it, offered burnt offerings and peace offerings, and blessed the people in the name of the Lord of hosts. He dealt to every one, both men and women, a cake of bread, a good piece of flesh, and a flagon of wine, and the people departed to their houses.

David returned to bless his own household, still in a good mood. Michal came out to meet him and said sarcastically, How glorious was the king of Israel today, who uncovered himself in the eyes of the handmaids as one of the vain fellows shamelessly uncovereth himself. She had watched from a distance and could think only of the king dancing with his clothes falling, when the Most High had just brought the ark of God back among Israel. She forgot the greatness of the day and let a murmuring spirit take her. David answered that he danced before the Lord who chose him before her father to be ruler over Israel, therefore he would play before the Lord, and would yet be more vile and base in his own sight, and of the maidservants he would be had in honor. Michal, the daughter of Saul, had no child unto the day of her death; the Lord shut her womb. Do not play with the Most High.

David consulted with the captains of thousands and hundreds and every leader, and proposed to all the congregation that they send abroad to their brethren everywhere, with the priests and Levites, to gather to them. His purpose was to bring again the ark of the Most High, for they had not inquired at it in the days of Saul. All the congregation agreed, for the thing was right in the eyes of all the people.

David gathered all Israel from Shihor of Egypt to the entering of Hemath to bring the ark from Kirjath-jearim, and went up to Baalah, which is Kirjath-jearim, belonging to Judah. They brought up the ark of the Most High, who dwelleth between the cherubims, carrying it in a new cart out of the house of Abinadab. David and all Israel played before the Most High with all their might, with singing, harps, psalteries, timbrels, cymbals, and trumpets, as they moved the ark to where David was so the priests could inquire. Do not let anyone claim the ark is in Ethiopia. The prophet Jeremiah hid the tabernacle, the ark, and the altar of incense in a cave, and it will not be found until the Most High gathers His people again. -

When they came to the threshingfloor of Chidon, the oxen stumbled and Uzza put forth his hand to hold the ark. The anger of the Most High was kindled against Uzza, and He smote him because he put his hand to the ark, and he died there before the Most High. The ark was only to be touched by the Levites; the Most High does not play. -

David was displeased that the Most High had made a breach upon Uzza, and that place was called Perez-uzza. David was afraid that day and asked how he could bring the ark home. David carried the ark aside into the house of Obed-edom the Gittite, where it remained three months, and the Most High blessed the house of Obed-edom and all that he had. The ark blesses when it is with Israel and afflicts those who wrongly hold it, as when the Philistines were struck with emerods for taking it. If it falls, let it fall, and get a Levite to lift it. -

*1 Concerning the divisions of the porters: Of the Korhites was Meshelemiah the son of Kore, of the sons of Asaph. 2 And the sons of Meshelemiah were, Zechariah the firstborn, Jediael the second, Zebadiah the third, Jathniel the fourth, 3 Elam the fifth, Jehohanan the sixth, Elioenai the seventh. 4 Moreover the sons of Obed-edom were, Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, and Sacar the fourth, and Nethaneel the fifth, 5 Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peulthai the eighth: for God blessed him. 6 Also unto Shemaiah his son were sons born, that ruled throughout the house of their father: for they were mighty men of valour. 7 The sons of Shemaiah; Othni, and Rephael, and Obed, Elzabad, whose brethren were strong men, Elihu, and Semachiah. 8 All these of the sons of Obed-edom: they and their sons and their brethren, able men for strength for the service, were threescore and two of Obed-edom. 9 And Meshelemiah had sons and brethren, strong men, eighteen. 10 Also Hosah, of the children of Merari, had sons; Simri the chief, (for though he was not the firstborn, yet his father made him the chief;) 11 Hilkiah the second, Tebaliah the third, Zechariah the fourth: all the sons and brethren of Hosah were thirteen. 12 Among these were the divisions of the porters, even among the chief men, having wards one against another, to minister in the house of the LORD. 13 And they cast lots, as well the small as the great, according to the house of their fathers, for every gate. 14 And the lot eastward fell to Shelemiah. Then for Zechariah his son, a wise counsellor, they cast lots; and his lot came out northward. 15 To Obed-edom southward; and to his sons the house of Asuppim. 16 To Shuppim and Hosah the lot came forth westward, with the gate Shallecheth, by the causeway of the going up, ward against ward. 17 Eastward were six Levites, northward four a day, southward four a day, and toward Asuppim two and two. 18 At Parbar westward, four at the causeway, and two at Parbar. 19 These are the divisions of the porters among the sons of Kore, and among the sons of Merari. 20 And of the Levites, Ahijah was over the treasures of the house of God, and over the treasures of the dedicated things. 21 As concerning the sons of Laadan; the sons of the Gershonite Laadan, chief fathers, even of Laadan the Gershonite, were Jehieli. 22 The sons of Jehieli; Zetham, and Joel his brother, which were over the treasures of the house of the LORD. 23 Of the Amramites, and the Izharites, the Hebronites, and the Uzzielites: 24 And Shebuel the son of Gershom, the son of Moses, was ruler of the treasures. 25 And his brethren by Eliezer; Rehabiah his son, and Jeshaiah his son, and Joram his son, and Zichri his son, and Shelomith his son. 26 Which Shelomith and his brethren were over all the treasures of the dedicated things, which David the king, and the chief fathers, the captains over thousands and hundreds, and the captains of the host, had dedicated. 27 Out of the spoils won in battles did they dedicate to maintain the house of the LORD. 28 And all that Samuel the seer, and Saul the son of Kish, and Abner the son of Ner, and Joab the son of Zeruiah, had dedicated; and whosoever had dedicated any thing, it was under the hand of Shelomith, and of his brethren. 29 Of the Izharites, Chenaniah and his sons were for the outward business over Israel, for officers and judges. 30 And of the Hebronites, Hashabiah and his brethren, men of valour, a thousand and seven hundred, were officers among them of Israel on this side Jordan westward in all the business of the LORD, and in the service of the king. 31 Among the Hebronites was Jerijah the chief, even among the Hebronites, according to the generations of his fathers. In the fortieth year of the reign of David they were sought for, and there were found among them mighty men of valour at Jazer of Gilead. 32 And his brethren, men of valour, were two thousand and seven hundred chief fathers, whom king David made rulers over the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half tribe of Manasseh, for every matter pertaining to God, and affairs of the king.*

David prepared a place and pitched a tent for the ark in the city of David. He declared that none ought to carry the ark but the Levites, for the Most High had chosen them to carry it and to minister unto him forever. -

David assembled all Israel and the chief Levites by their families, naming the sons of Kohath, Merari, Gershom, Elizaphan, Hebron, and Uzziel with their chiefs and numbers. He called for the priests Zadok and Abiathar and for the Levites, showing the Most High had set a clear structure among the priesthood.

David charged the chief fathers of the Levites to sanctify themselves before bringing up the ark, because the first attempt failed when they did not seek him after the due order. The Levites bore the ark upon their shoulders with the staves, as Moses commanded according to the word of the Most High. -

David appointed Levites as singers with psalteries, harps, and cymbals, to lift up the voice with joy. Heman, Asaph, and Ethan were appointed to sound cymbals of brass; others played harps and psalteries; the priests blew the trumpets before the ark, and doorkeepers were set. Every rank had its assigned place.

David and the elders and captains went to bring up the ark from the house of Obededom with joy. When the Most High helped the Levites bearing the ark, they offered seven bullocks and seven rams. David was clothed in a robe of fine linen along with the Levites and singers, and wore an ephod of linen. The people were dressed well, and the same custom carried down through Solomon.

All Israel brought up the ark with shouting, cornet, trumpets, cymbals, psalteries, and harps. Michal the daughter of Saul looked out the window and despised David in her heart as he danced and played. In the midst of pure righteousness she was out of the spirit, hating him instead of rejoicing.

Blessed is every one that feareth the Lord, that walketh in his ways, walking in God's commandments. When we walk in the laws of the Lord we are undefiled; when we do not, we are defiled. For thou shalt eat the labor of thine hands. There is profit in laboring, and this is not just the nine to five, it is laboring in this truth. We have too many people in IUIC who just talk and do not labor at all, and shame on you. You will escape this world by your works. -
Happy shalt thou be, and it shall be well with thee. This blessing follows the man who fears the Lord and walks in his ways, eating the labor of his own hands.

Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine. Jump back to [Psalms 127:3](/bible/psalms/127#v3), for the wife is that fruitful vine, the fruit of the womb that is his reward. Your wife will be a fruitful possession producing many children. Thy children like olive plants round about thy table. Our children will grow up full-grown in this truth; our sons honored in the age of wisdom, our daughters precious cornerstones, polished daughters of Sarah, eloquent as in the days of old. -
Behold, thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the Lord. A man will be blessed with blessed children if he fears the Lord.
The Lord shall bless thee out of Zion, and thou shalt see the good of Jerusalem all the days of thy life.

Yea, thou shalt see thy children's children, and peace upon Israel. There are plenty of benefits to keeping God's laws and being blessed. Job is an example. Job was tried by the Lord in the first chapters, and he was blessed in his latter end, living to see four generations of his children. -

verses.text: And when they came to Nachon’s threshingfloor, Uzzah put forth his hand to the ark of God, and took hold of it; for the oxen shook it.
And the anger of the Lord was kindled against Uzzah; and God smote him there for his error; and there he died by the ark of God.
And David was displeased, because the Lord had made a breach upon Uzzah: and he called the name of the place Perez–uzzah to this day.
And David was afraid of the Lord that day, and said, How shall the ark of the Lord come to me?
So David would not remove the ark of the Lord unto him into the city of David: but David carried it aside into the house of Obed–edom the Gittite.
And the ark of the Lord continued in the house of Obed–edom the Gittite three months: and the Lord blessed Obed–edom, and all his household.

And it was told king David, saying, The Lord hath blessed the house of Obed–edom, and all that pertaineth unto him, because of the ark of God. So David went and brought up the ark of God from the house of Obed–edom into the city of David with gladness.
So David brought not the ark home to himself to the city of David, but carried it aside into the house of Obed–edom the Gittite.
And the ark of God remained with the family of Obed–edom in his house three months. And the Lord blessed the house of Obed–edom, and all that he had.
Moreover the sons of Obed–edom were, Shemaiah the firstborn, Jehozabad the second, Joah the third, and Sacar the fourth, and Nethaneel the fifth,
Ammiel the sixth, Issachar the seventh, Peulthai the eighth: for God blessed him.
Also unto Shemaiah his son were sons born, that ruled throughout the house of their father: for they were mighty men of valour.
The sons of Shemaiah; Othni, and Rephael, and Obed, Elzabad, whose brethren were strong men, Elihu, and Semachiah.
All these of the sons of Obed–edom: they and their sons and their brethren, able men for strength for the service, were threescore and two of Obed–edom.

And Shebaniah, and Jehoshaphat, and Nethaneel, and Amasai, and Zechariah, and Benaiah, and Eliezer, the priests, did blow with the trumpets before the ark of God: and Obed–edom and Jehiah were doorkeepers for the ark.
So David, and the elders of Israel, and the captains over thousands, went to bring up the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the house of Obed–edom with joy.
Blessed is every one that feareth the Lord; that walketh in his ways.
For thou shalt eat the labour of thine hands: happy shalt thou be, and it shall be well with thee.
Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine by the sides of thine house: thy children like olive plants round about thy table.
Behold, that thus shall the man be blessed that feareth the Lord.
